    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>

        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

The fix strategy for the `tools.jar` issue: Add an exclusion for `com.sun:tools` from the `compile-testing` dependency in each module POM. On Java 9+, the compiler classes are part of the JDK module system and no longer need `tools.jar`.

input.content:
# Maven Dependency Exclusions

## Problem: Transitive System-Scoped Dependencies

When a dependency declares a `system`-scoped transitive dependency (like `com.sun:tools`),
Maven resolves it at build time even if it's only needed at test scope. If the system path
doesn't exist (e.g., `tools.jar` on Java 9+), the build fails.

## Solution: Exclude the Transitive Dependency

Add an `<exclusions>` block to the dependency declaration in your POM:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.7</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

## Why This Works

On Java 9+, the classes formerly in `tools.jar` (like `javax.tools.JavaCompiler`)
are part of the `java.compiler` module and available on the module path by default.
The `com.sun:tools` system dependency is unnecessary and its `systemPath` points
to a file that no longer exists.

## Key Points

- `<exclusions>` are added to the dependency that *transitively* brings in the unwanted artifact
- The `<groupId>` and `<artifactId>` inside `<exclusion>` identify the artifact to exclude
- No `<version>` is needed inside `<exclusion>`
- This approach preserves all other transitive dependencies

```xml
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

## Why This Works

On Java 9+, the classes formerly in `tools.jar` (like `javax.tools.JavaCompiler`)
are part of the `java.compiler` module and available on the module path by default.
The `com.sun:tools` system dependency is unnecessary and its `systemPath` points
to a file that no longer exists.

## Key Points

- `<exclusions>` are added to the dependency that *transitively* brings in the unwanted artifact
- The `<groupId>` and `<artifactId>` inside `<exclusion>` identify the artifact to exclude
- No `<version>` is needed inside `<exclusion>`
- This approach preserves all other transitive dependencies

# Java tools.jar Migration (Java 8 to 9+)

## Background

In Java 8 and earlier, the Java compiler API classes were packaged in `tools.jar`,
located at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar`. Many projects declared a system-scoped
dependency on this JAR:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>${java.version}</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

## What Changed in Java 9+

Java 9 introduced the module system (Project Jigsaw). The `tools.jar` file was
eliminated and its contents distributed across modules:

- `java.compiler` - javax.tools.* (JavaCompiler, etc.)
- `jdk.compiler` - com.sun.tools.javac.* (internal compiler API)
- `jdk.javadoc` - javadoc tool classes

These modules are available by default on the module path.

## Common Error

```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.x at specified path
/path/to/jdk/../lib/tools.jar
```

## Solutions

### 1. Exclude from Transitive Dependencies
If `tools.jar` comes transitively from another dependency:
```xml
<exclusions>
  <exclusion>
    <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
    <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  </exclusion>
</exclusions>
```

### 2. Add a Java 9+ Profile
If `tools.jar` is a direct dependency, make it conditional:
```xml
<profiles>
  <profile>
    <id>java8-and-earlier</id>
    <activation>
      <jdk>[,9)</jdk>
    </activation>
    <dependencies>
      <dependency>
        <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
        <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
        <version>${java.version}</version>
        <scope>system</scope>
        <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
      </dependency>
    </dependencies>
  </profile>
</profiles>
```

### 3. Update the Library
Libraries like `compile-testing` eventually removed the `tools.jar` dependency
in later versions. Upgrading may resolve the issue.

# Maven Multi-Module Project Builds

## Structure

A multi-module Maven project has:
- A parent POM with `<packaging>pom</packaging>`
- Child modules referenced via `<modules>` section
- Each module has its own `pom.xml` with a `<parent>` reference

## Building

### Full Build
```bash
mvn -f build-pom.xml verify
```

### Build Specific Module
```bash
cd module-dir && mvn compile
```

### Build with Aggregator POM
```bash
mvn -f build-pom.xml compile -pl module1,module2
```

## Common Issues

### SNAPSHOT Dependencies Between Modules
When module B depends on module A's SNAPSHOT version, module A must be
`mvn install`-ed first so its artifact is in the local repository:
```bash
cd module-a && mvn install -DskipTests
cd module-b && mvn compile
```

### Parent POM Not Found
If the parent POM is a SNAPSHOT version, install it first:
```bash
mvn install -N  # Install only the parent POM (non-recursive)
```

## Key Maven Flags

- `-B` - Batch mode (non-interactive)
- `-U` - Force update of snapshots
- `-DskipTests` - Skip test execution
- `-Dcheckstyle.skip=true` - Skip checkstyle
- `--fail-at-end` - Continue building after failures
- `-pl module1,module2` - Build only specified modules

# Creating Git/GNU Diff Patch Files

## Standard Unified Diff Format

The standard unified diff format is used by both `git diff` and GNU `diffutils`.

### Format Structure

```diff
--- a/path/to/original/file
+++ b/path/to/modified/file
@@ -start,count +start,count @@ optional context
 unchanged line
-removed line
+added line
 unchanged line
```

### Key Elements

1. **File headers**: `---` for original, `+++` for modified
2. **Hunk headers**: `@@ -old_start,old_count +new_start,new_count @@`
3. **Context lines**: Prefixed with space (` `)
4. **Removed lines**: Prefixed with minus (`-`)
5. **Added lines**: Prefixed with plus (`+`)

### Example

```diff
--- a/common/pom.xml
+++ b/common/pom.xml
@@ -54,6 +54,11 @@
       <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
       <version>0.7</version>
       <scope>test</scope>
+      <exclusions>
+        <exclusion>
+          <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
+          <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
+        </exclusion>
+      </exclusions>
     </dependency>
```

## Applying Patches

### Using git apply
```bash
git apply patch_1.diff
```

### Using patch command
```bash
patch -p1 < patch_1.diff
```

### Options
- `-p1` - Strip one leading path component (removes `a/` or `b/` prefix)
- `--check` - Dry run to test if patch applies cleanly
- `-R` - Reverse the patch

## Creating Patches from Git

```bash
# Unstaged changes
git diff > changes.diff

# Staged changes
git diff --cached > staged.diff

# Between commits
git diff commit1 commit2 > between.diff

# For a specific file
git diff -- path/to/file > file.diff
```

## .travis.yml for Java Projects

```yaml
language: java

jdk:
  - oraclejdk7
  - openjdk7

install:
  - mvn -B dependency:go-offline

  - mvn -B verify

branches:
  except:

```

## Common Issues

### File Reference Typos
Ensure file references in `.travis.yml` match actual filenames:
- `build.pom.xml` vs `build-pom.xml` (dot vs hyphen)

### JDK Compatibility
Projects configured for older JDKs (e.g., Java 6/7) may fail when
Travis upgrades to newer JDK versions because:
1. `tools.jar` doesn't exist in Java 9+
2. Source level 1.5 is unsupported in Java 12+
3. Source level 1.6 is unsupported in Java 12+
4. Internal APIs may have been removed or encapsulated

### Maven Build Flags
- `-B` - Batch mode (required for CI, no interactive prompts)
- `-U` - Force SNAPSHOT updates
- `--fail-at-end` - Don't stop at first module failure
- `--fail-never` - Never fail the build (used in dependency resolution)
- `-DskipTests=true` - Skip test execution
- `-Dsource.skip=true` - Skip source JAR creation
- `-Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true` - Skip Javadoc generation

BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS: google/auto
=====================================

Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
Build System: Maven (multi-module)
Java Version: 11.0.27 (OpenJDK, JRE-only install)
Maven Version: 3.6.3

Modules: common, factory, service, value
Build Command: mvn -B -U -f build-pom.xml verify --fail-at-end

=== ROOT CAUSE ===

ERROR: com.sun:tools:jar dependency resolution failure

All four modules (common, factory, service, value) depend on
the `compile-testing` library (versions 0.6, 0.7, or 0.8) for testing.
All versions of `compile-testing` declare a system-scoped dependency on:

    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
      <version>${java.version}</version>
      <scope>system</scope>
      <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
    </dependency>

This references tools.jar which existed in Java 8 and earlier at
$JAVA_HOME/../lib/tools.jar. In Java 9+ (including Java 11 used here),
tools.jar was eliminated as part of Project Jigsaw (module system).

The error message:
  "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
   /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

This blocks ALL compilation, causing the entire build to fail at the
very first module (common).

=== ERROR TYPE ===

Build configuration / dependency resolution error.
NOT a source code error.

=== AFFECTED FILES ===

1. common/pom.xml  - compile-testing 0.7 brings in com.sun:tools
2. service/pom.xml - compile-testing 0.6 brings in com.sun:tools
3. factory/pom.xml - compile-testing 0.8 brings in com.sun:tools
4. value/pom.xml   - compile-testing 0.6 brings in com.sun:tools

=== FIX PLAN ===

Add <exclusions> for com.sun:tools to each compile-testing dependency
declaration in all four module POM files. On Java 9+, the compiler
classes (javax.tools.*) are part of the java.compiler module and are
available by default without tools.jar.

The fix for each module POM:

    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>X.Y</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
      <exclusions>
        <exclusion>
          <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
          <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
        </exclusion>
      </exclusions>
    </dependency>

=== VERIFICATION ===

After applying the exclusion to common/pom.xml, the common module
compiled successfully (BUILD SUCCESS) with only deprecation warnings
(SimpleElementVisitor6, SimpleTypeVisitor6 - expected on Java 11).

=== PATCH FILES TO CREATE ===

patch_1.diff - common/pom.xml exclusion
patch_2.diff - service/pom.xml exclusion
patch_3.diff - factory/pom.xml exclusion
patch_4.diff - value/pom.xml exclusion

compiled successfully (BUILD SUCCESS) with only deprecation warnings
